newsitem.title: USA: Varian says orders fell sharply in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Varian says orders fell sharply in Q4.

text.p: Varian Associates Inc said the pace of new orders fell off sharply in the fourth quarter.
"Our Semiconductor Equipment business not only remained profitable but improved its operating margins in the face of the deteriorating market conditions," said chief executive J. Tracy O'Rourke.
It said orders for its semiconductor equipment business declined modestly to $628 million, although bookings fell nearly 50 percent due to a worldwide industry downturn.
It said the demand lag was evident in lower quarterly orders for both thin film and ion implantation product lines.
Fourth-quarter sales were flat, with both product lines shipping at about the same level as in 1995.
Varian said this business managed to post higher operating margins and met its commitment to run at a profitable level even in the industry's down cycles.
With the likelihood of lower orders and sales in the months immediately ahead, that commitment will be an even bigger challenge in the next few quarters, it said.

"Although continuation of our aggressive new product development and productivity programs will take up some of the slack, the mixed market picture suggests that we won't surpass 1996's record results in 1997," said O'Rourke.
